title: KB3k: demote the mu2-constant even-half condition; (4,2) walk shard 29 (outcome=partial)
body:
# KB3k: the mu2-constant even-half condition for the 18-point cover question of F2^7

Set-level only, no words enumerated. Outcome = partial. The `mu2` "constant per
split" lead of #3108 (agent-83) is pressed. It is not a law of the covering
condition: `mu2` varies at a single minimal split, `(4,4)` in `F2^3`, and the
variation is explained exactly. For the both-odd target splits `(11,7)`/`(9,9)`,
`mu2` is constant at every scale where covers can be produced, but that is
CHECKED, not forced, and it is not a proof filter. The lead is therefore
demoted. No class is decided; no cover is constructed; no false kill.

Author: Aaron Wang, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no model
named; no independent human review claimed).

## Object and chain

In the PR943 prefix-walk model (#943, Ross Richardson) a restored seven-source
singleton word is universal exactly when its prefix set `P` covers: `P + P =
F2^7`. The 17-point question is closed (#2542, #2634, #2773, #2870); #2911
narrowed the 18-point question to `(12,6)`, `(11,7)`, `(10,8)`, `(9,9)`; #2933
classified the vanishing configurations; #2961 excluded `(10,8)` and decided the
three tightest classes; #3023 killed `(12,6)` A-vanish `(5,1)` and reduced
`(4,2)`/`(3,3)` to walkable forms; #3034 demoted the parity shortcut and
localized the m=5 obstruction; #3108 ran a partial `(4,2)` walk, classified the
even-half self-sum profiles, and recorded the `mu2`-constancy lead this PR
presses. The reduced covering object (#2911 reduction lemma): for `G = F2^m`, a
pair `(A, B)` covers iff `A + B = G` (cross) and `(A+A) u (B+B) = G` (even-half).
A `P + P = F2^{m+1}` cover with parity split `(s,t)` is exactly a reduced
`(A,B)` cover of `F2^m` with `|A| = s, |B| = t`. The 18-point question is the
reduced cover of `F2^6` (64 elements).

Every cited PR author was re-verified at writing with `gh pr view NNN --json
author,title`: #2542/#2634/#2773/#2870/#2911/#2933/#2961/#3023/#3034/#3108 are
Aaron Wang (navinor); #2691/#2973 are Nicholas Stone (NicholasStone); #3005 is
Nick Petalas (petalas); #1185 is Mister-Meeseeks. This PR is strictly SET-level
and enumerates no words (Nicholas Stone's `22 <= f(7) <= 24` word line, #2973 /
#3005, is untouched).

## The exact identity (PROVEN)

For any reduced cover `(A,B)` of `G = F2^m`, inclusion-exclusion on
`(A+A) u (B+B) = G` gives `mu2 = |(A+A) n (B+B)| = |A+A| + |B+B| - |G|`. So
`mu2` is constant per split `(a,b)` if and only if the selfsum-size sum
`|A+A| + |B+B|` is constant per split. The identity holds at 0 violations over
all 41,341 `F2^3` covers and all `F2^4` covers checked.

## Not forced: the minimal variation split is (4,4) in F2^3 (PROVEN)

Complete enumeration at `F2^1`, `F2^2`, `F2^3` shows `mu2` is constant per split
at `F2^1` and `F2^2`, and first varies at `F2^3` at split `(4,4)`. This is the
minimal variation split.

| Group | Split | Covers | mu2 values | sum of selfsums |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F2^3 | (4,4) | 3,360 | 3 and 6 | 11 and 14 |
| F2^3 | (4,k) or (k,4), k=5..8 | 560 to 3,920 | 4 and 7 | 12 and 15 |
| F2^4 | (2,8) | 15,360 | 1 | 17 |
| F2^4 | (4,6) | 143,360 | 4 | 20 |

Mechanism (exact): `mu2` varies with the additive structure of a half. In
`F2^3` a 4-set is either a coset of a 2-dim subspace (an affine plane,
`|A+A| = 4`) or generic (`|A+A| = 7`). At `(4,4)` the halves vary independently.

| half A | half B | selfsums | sum | mu2 | covers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| generic | generic | 7, 7 | 14 | 6 | 2,688 |
| plane | generic | 4, 7 | 11 | 3 | 336 |
| generic | plane | 7, 4 | 11 | 3 | 336 |
| plane | plane | n/a | n/a | n/a | 0 (never covers) |

So `mu2 = 6 - 3 * (number of plane halves)`: one structured (affine-plane) half
lowers `|A+A|` by 3 and `mu2` by 3. The covering condition does not pin this. At
`(4,6)` in `F2^4` the split is constant again (`mu2 = 4`) only because the two
selfsum sizes are anti-correlated by the cover condition (`|A+A| = 4` forces
`|B+B| = 16`; `|A+A| = 7` forces `|B+B| = 13`; the sum stays 20). So the
constancy that survives is a correlation of a particular split, not a covering
law.

## The both-odd regime of (11,7)/(9,9) (CHECKED, not forced)

The target splits `(11,7)` and `(9,9)` are both-odd. At every both-odd split
where covers can be produced, `mu2` is constant: `F2^3` both-odd splits
(complete), and `F2^5 (7,7)` (310 covers, all `mu2 = 12` with both selfsums
pinned at 22). But this is not forced. The `(4,4)` `F2^3` counterexample shows
the covering condition does not pin `mu2` in general, and both-odd halves at
`F2^6` (`|A| = 11, 9`) can still have varying `|A+A|` (a subspace plus points).
Direct `F2^6 (9,9)`/`(11,7)` covers were not produced in a bounded hill-climbing
search (0 in 300 restarts each), so `mu2` variation at the exact target splits is
neither observed nor ruled out.

Verdict: `mu2`-constancy is scale- and split-dependent, false for both-even
splits, empirical for both-odd splits, unforced everywhere. The planned lift
("carry `mu2` = const to #2911's 501/196 rows as a filter, then lift to m=6") is
not justified and is demoted. This is the same shape as the demoted
scale-dependent self-sum lift of #3034. (PR 2911's 501/196 rows are
pair-representation row configurations, not concrete `(A,B)` covers, so `mu2`
cannot be evaluated on them without the still-open row-to-cover map.)

## The (4,2) walk (continuation)

The `(12,6)` A-vanish `(4,2)` decision walk is continued as a budget-honest
partial, never an exclusion. #3108's sharded walk is extended by shard 29 with a
per-shard receipt (explicit `complete`/`budget_hit` flags, budget checked after
every U). This session's shard ran from empty receipts and was re-run from empty
receipts with identical counters to prove recomputation. The inherited 29 shards
plus shard 29 give 30 of 2048 shards complete, 2,490 U slices, 257,845,500
normalized pairs, `w_candidates = 0` and `covering_configs = 0` on every walked
pair. The complete walk is far outside one session (#3108 sized it at ~608
core-hours), so this is a narrowed remainder.

## Reproduce

Standard library only, CPython 3.12. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-mu2-evenhalf-kb3k-88a1/verify.py quick
python3 -I -B research/f7-mu2-evenhalf-kb3k-88a1/mu2_search.py m3
python3 -I -B research/f7-mu2-evenhalf-kb3k-88a1/mu2_mechanism.py
```

Markers: `PASS_KB3K_QUICK`, `MU2_M3_DONE`, `MU2_MINIMALITY_DONE`. Heavier
receipts re-run with `mu2_search.py m4`, `mu2_search.py m5odd`,
`mu2_search.py m6`, `mu2_odd_search.py`. All arithmetic is exact Python integers.
Vendored predecessor engines are byte-exact with SHA-256 pins in `SOURCES.json`.

## Scope and limitations

Set-level only inside PR943's abstract interface. The verdict is that
`mu2`-constancy is not a covering law and is demoted as a proof filter; it is
not a proof that `(11,7)`/`(9,9)` are excluded, and no cover is constructed or
excluded here. `(4,4)` variation is PROVEN (complete `F2^3`); both-odd
constancy is CHECKED at `F2^3` (complete) and `F2^5 (7,7)` (310 covers) only;
`F2^6 (9,9)`/`(11,7)` `mu2` is untested (no covers produced). Not checked:
anything word-level (#2973/#3005 hold `22 <= f(7) <= 24`), the row-to-cover map,
the `(12,6)` D-vanish classes, the surviving `(10,8)` classes, the 19-point
question, and any kappa, supplier or selected-frontier implication. Frontiers
unchanged.
